contract: Coarsest common labeled probabilistic bisimulation of a supplied empirical action/state model for every fixed source-withdrawal set. Missing observations produce an observable unknown result. The partition must be valid uniformly; this does not claim the smallest separately chosen quotient for each withdrawal set.
candidate: Refine observable-label blocks by exact Boolean-polynomial equivalence of every action's transition probabilities into the current blocks, including unknown support.
controls: independent enumeration of all set partitions and raw rational probabilities on small models
shared per-outcome decision diagrams in both fixed source orders
direct source-normalized comparison, complete for exactly one source per observation, with constant-distribution support simplification for joint sources
current-evidence-only merging as a negative control

correlated.construction: Even states retain base source histograms; odd states multiply them by surviving-source count. Target state identity varies while target label follows source/action parity.

independentHistories.construction: Every state/action pair has its own source; current distributions agree by label but evidence availability differs under withdrawals.

acceptance: Exact candidate/independent-oracle/diagram partition agreement wherever each control completes; original and quotient transition distributions agree in every checked withdrawal; sequential retraction and re-minimization from the quotient agrees with fresh minimization of surviving observations. Record the no-compaction stress case and the current-only negative control. Preserve raw models, partitions, checks and serialized sizes.
accounting: Packet bytes include quotient records, labels, dimensions and the map for every original state. These are serialized bytes, not whole-process memory or reader tokens. Original episodic records are not reconstructable from the declared readout; applications requiring them must retain and charge them separately.
promotion: No system promotion: the constructed source correlations and supplied state labels still require a real behavioral workload and comparison with established parametric algebra tools.
